issues.title: Reposition away from "profile of AIMS" to only having "relationship to AIMS", and revisit Table of Contents
issues.author: pcarleton
issues.body:
This draft does fit the conceptual model put forward in [AIMS](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-klrc-aiagent-auth/), however calling it a "profile" doesn't quite fit.

This issue is to track revising the draft to be less dependent on AIMS, so it needs:
* to remove "profile" language
* to revisit the concepts section to be able to stand by itself more readily

Once this issue is complete, the following should be true:
* A reader does not need to read all of AIMS to make use of this draft
* A reader familiar with AIMS should know how this draft lines up with its conceptual model of agents as workloads

comments.author: PieterKas
comments.body:
Nice! Great to see the Privacy Considerations in there :)

Building on the above,  maybe we can: 

1. Make the **Workload Authorization Grant** section more focused and constrain it to the Grant format and processing (including claims)
2. Move anything to do with the AS to an **Authorization Server Processing** to it's own section (allows us to focus changes for AS's in one place)
3. Break out **Trust Establishment** as its own section (we can set the context for why it is needed with a diagram under Concepts/Overview, along with a typical mermaid diagram showing the flows e2e)?

issues.title: Pick small set of standard claims
issues.author: pcarleton
issues.body:
We want:
* A small set of claims that are common among implementations (target: max of 3)
* extensibility to add more claims if a platform and resource want
* Clearly specify which claims can be trusted for policy decisions, and clarify that others cannot
* ability to re-use existing authz modeling where appropriate (i.e. I want this agent to have the same permissions as humans on this team)

The leading candidate is `roles`, `groups` and `entitlements` from https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7643#section-4.1.2 / https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9068#section-2.2.3.1

If that does end up being what we do, we need to:
* play out an example of the agent platform giving claims like roles / groups if they're not specific to the platform
* decide whether they need to be namespaced by FQDN (or if issuer namespacing is sufficient)
* explain relationship to #3

comments.author: PieterKas
comments.body:
It may be good to elaborate on the problem we are trying to solve by picking any additional claims beyond what is defined in RFC 7523 and/or ID-JAG? What is the specific use case?

My first instinct is that we should not make any claims beyond what is needed by RFC 7523 REQUIRED in this draft. That would maximise compatibility with existing infrastructure and minimise the assumptions about the deployment. What mandatory values would we need beyond what is described already?

For the examples of roles, groups and entitlements my concern would be that values for those claims are things that may have meaning on one platform, but once you cross a trust boundary, it may have different meaning in a different domain. It also assumes a certain kind of underlying RBAC system, which although common, may not be universal.

In terms of optional claims, the three claims you describe feel like something that falls under the ID-JAG "authorization_details" claim and can be described in a RAR object (which may still need to be defined, but perhaps that is something that gets profiled elsewhere?).

I am also curious about the choice of picking values from SCIM as claims - is there specific upside we expect from that (other than these values matching attributes provisioned for users through SICM)?

issues.title: Discuss integration points with enterprise IdP (proposal: out of scope for this draft)
issues.author: pcarleton
issues.body:
This draft currently aims to be as simple as possible and targeted at an agent platform issuing its own tokens, similar to how a k8s cluster has an OIDC provider that's trusted in some WIF implementations today.

However, there is a deployment model that could make sense here where folks want their enterprise IdP to be the single source of truth into what has access into their system, e.g. to revoke an agent's access in the IdP instead of needing to go to the agent platform.

The rough shape that seems most promising here is:
* The agent platform is trusted by the IdP to create agent identities
* The resource authorization server trusts the IdP
* The IdP is responsible for ensuring groups / roles / entitlements align with the organization-wide authz model

This has a few implications:
* The agent platform needs to exchange its platform-issued token for one issued by the IdP
* The agent platform still provides the `client_assertion` to prove the request is coming from the platform
* the IdP *may* choose to do a SCIM operation or other lifecycle management into the resource authorization server if it needs to
  * this implies that the token exchange may need to be asynchronous if a stateful provisioning is happening
* the resource authorization server may want to rely on a stateful provisioning process
 
I'm proposing this IdP-integrated deployment model can be lightly mentioned in this draft, but the WAG draft keeps "how does the agent get its authorization grant" out of scope.  (i.e. an IdP-integrated deployment would be in a separate draft).

Also note, this deployment model looks very similar to ID-JAG's typical model, with a small variation: rather than an id_token issued by the IdP in its token exchange, the IdP would be accepting a token from the agent platform itself (likely a WAG).  This is also related to: https://github.com/oauth-wg/oauth-identity-assertion-authz-grant/issues/73

pulls.title: Clarify property assertion and freshness semantics
pulls.author: FutureEnterprises
pulls.body:
Addresses the trust-boundary portion of #2.

This change separates three facts that the current text places close together:

- An Agent Property is an issuer assertion made when the grant is issued.
- `iat` and `exp` establish the grant's age and acceptance window, not whether mutable state is still true later.
- Roles, groups, entitlements, and similar values are interpreted through the Resource Server's issuer-scoped local mapping. They are not portable permission assignments.

If a policy requires a Property to remain true at presentation or access time, the deployment must obtain evidence current for that time. Otherwise, grant and access-token lifetimes bound the stale-claim exposure.

This does not choose the final property vocabulary, require a specific status mechanism, or add an EMILIA dependency.

Verification:

- `make` completed successfully.
- The existing EMILIA WAG-to-AEB composition fixture reproduced 15 of 15 checks against the pinned WAG-00 source.
